title: Equal1, NVIDIA, and Dell Technologies Demonstrate Real-Time Hybrid Quantum-Classical Rack Integration at SC26 - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Equal1, NVIDIA and Dell demonstrated an integrated hybrid quantum-classical rack at SC26, pairing Equal1's 1.6 kW rack-mounted RacQ silicon quantum computer with Dell servers, NVIDIA Ising Calibration models and NVQLink, orchestrated by Dell's Quantum Intelligent Orchestrator prototype.

insights.claim: At SC26 in Chicago, Equal1 demonstrated its 1.6 kW rack-mounted RacQ silicon spin-qubit quantum computer integrated with Dell Technologies data center servers inside a standard rack footprint.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Low-power, standard-rack quantum hardware lowers data-center integration barriers — relevant to Dell's positioning in quantum-ready infrastructure.

insights.claim: Hybrid execution across Equal1's quantum hardware and classical servers is coordinated by the Dell Quantum Intelligent Orchestrator (QIO) software prototype.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Dell building its own quantum orchestration layer signals intent to own the hybrid workflow stack; still a prototype.
insights.locator: Hybrid execution across the classical and quantum hardware

themes.theme: NVIDIA's quantum software and interconnect role

insights.claim: The Equal1–NVIDIA–Dell stack uses NVIDIA Ising Calibration open models for automated gate tuning, including real-time controlled-Z gate calibration, and NVIDIA NVQLink for ultra-low-latency quantum-processor-to-GPU round-trip communication.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NVIDIA keeps embedding itself as the classical control/AI layer across multiple qubit modalities, extending GPU demand into quantum.
insights.locator: The joint software and interconnect stack
